claims.title: Ingólfr Arnarson settles Reykjavík
claims.summary: By tradition the first permanent settler, Ingólfr Arnarson, came from Norway around 874 and established his homestead at the site he named Reykjavík, opening the age of settlement, the Landnám.

sources.label: The Discovery and Settlement of Iceland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-874-ingolfr-arnarson-settles-reykjavik, claim TL:ISL:event:874:ingolfr-arnarson-settles-reykjavik, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Landnám (Age of Settlement)
claims.summary: Within roughly sixty years hundreds of Norse settlers, many by way of the Norse colonies in the British Isles, claimed Iceland's habitable land, as recorded in Íslendingabók and Landnámabók.

sources.label: The Discovery and Settlement of Iceland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-870-the-landnam-age-of-settlement, claim TL:ISL:event:870:the-landnam-age-of-settlement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Althing at Þingvellir
claims.summary: The settlers established a general assembly, the Althing, on the plain of Þingvellir, where law was recited from the Law Rock; it is one of the oldest parliaments in the world and the centre of the Icelandic Commonwealth.

sources.label: History of Þingvellir and the Alþing
The Discovery and Settlement of Iceland

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-930-founding-of-the-althing-at-ingvellir, claim TL:ISL:event:930:founding-of-the-althing-at-ingvellir, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Icelandic Commonwealth
claims.summary: A stateless society of chieftains and farmers governed itself for over three centuries through the Althing and its law council, without a king or central executive.

sources.label: History of Þingvellir and the Alþing

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-930-the-icelandic-commonwealth, claim TL:ISL:event:930:the-icelandic-commonwealth, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Althing adopts Christianity
claims.summary: Faced with a split between pagans and Christians, the Althing entrusted the decision to the lawspeaker Þorgeir, who ruled that Iceland should become Christian; the conversion was achieved by compromise, without bloodshed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1000-the-althing-adopts-christianity, claim TL:ISL:event:1000:the-althing-adopts-christianity, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Snorri Sturluson and the sagas
claims.summary: Chieftain and twice lawspeaker, Snorri Sturluson wrote the Prose Edda and the Heimskringla, central works of the saga age that preserved the mythology and history of the Norse world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1179-snorri-sturluson-and-the-sagas, claim TL:ISL:event:1179:snorri-sturluson-and-the-sagas, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Age of the Sturlungs
claims.summary: Rivalry among a few powerful families, above all the Sturlungs, brought decades of feud, killing and burning, fatally weakening the Commonwealth's institutions of consensus.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1220-the-age-of-the-sturlungs, claim TL:ISL:event:1220:the-age-of-the-sturlungs, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Old Covenant (Gamli sáttmáli)
claims.summary: Worn down by civil strife and pressed by King Haakon IV, the Icelandic chieftains swore allegiance to the Norwegian crown, ending the independent Commonwealth and beginning centuries of foreign rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1262-the-old-covenant-gamli-sattmali, claim TL:ISL:event:1262:the-old-covenant-gamli-sattmali, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Execution of Bishop Jón Arason
claims.summary: Jón Arason, bishop of Hólar and the last Catholic bishop in Iceland, was beheaded with his two sons at Skálholt for resisting the Danish-imposed Reformation, after which Iceland became fully Lutheran.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1550-execution-of-bishop-jon-arason, claim TL:ISL:event:1550:execution-of-bishop-jon-arason, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Danish trade monopoly
claims.summary: The Danish crown confined all Icelandic trade to a small group of licensed Danish merchants, depressing prices and returns and impoverishing the island for nearly two centuries.

sources.label: History of Iceland, 1840s to the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1602-the-danish-trade-monopoly, claim TL:ISL:event:1602:the-danish-trade-monopoly, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Laki eruption
claims.summary: The Laki fissure erupted for eight months from June 1783, producing about 14.7 cubic kilometres of lava and immense quantities of toxic gas that poisoned the land and spread a haze across Europe.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1783-the-laki-eruption, claim TL:ISL:event:1783:the-laki-eruption, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Móðuharðindin famine
claims.summary: Fallout from Laki killed most of Iceland's livestock; the ensuing 'famine of the mist' killed roughly a fifth of the population, the worst disaster in the country's history.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1783-the-mo-uhar-indin-famine, claim TL:ISL:event:1783:the-mo-uhar-indin-famine, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Althing restored
claims.summary: A royal decree of 1843 revived the Althing, which first met again on 1 July 1845 as an advisory assembly, reviving in modern form the institution founded in 930.

sources.label: History of Iceland, 1840s to the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1843-the-althing-restored, claim TL:ISL:event:1843:the-althing-restored, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Constitution on the settlement millennium
claims.summary: On the thousandth anniversary of the settlement, Denmark granted Iceland a constitution and increased control over domestic affairs, though executive power remained with the crown.

sources.label: History of Iceland, 1840s to the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1874-constitution-on-the-settlement-millennium, claim TL:ISL:event:1874:constitution-on-the-settlement-millennium, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Home Rule
claims.summary: Iceland gained Home Rule, with an Icelandic minister resident in Reykjavík and answerable to the Althing, a major step toward full self-government.

sources.label: History of Iceland, 1840s to the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1904-home-rule, claim TL:ISL:event:1904:home-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Act of Union and the Kingdom of Iceland
claims.summary: The Danish-Icelandic Act of Union made Iceland a sovereign state in personal union with the Danish crown, with Denmark retaining foreign affairs and the union open to termination after twenty-five years.

sources.label: History of Iceland, 1840s to the Second World War

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1918-the-act-of-union-and-the-kingdom-of-iceland, claim TL:ISL:event:1918:the-act-of-union-and-the-kingdom-of-iceland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: British occupation of Iceland
claims.summary: After Germany occupied Denmark, British forces occupied strategically vital Iceland in May 1940 to forestall a German move, severing Iceland's last constitutional ties to its monarch.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1940-british-occupation-of-iceland, claim TL:ISL:event:1940:british-occupation-of-iceland, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: United States assumes Iceland's defence
claims.summary: By agreement with the Icelandic government, the United States took over the island's defence in 1941, building a substantial military presence in the North Atlantic.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1949, Vol. IV (Iceland and the North Atlantic Treaty)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1941-united-states-assumes-iceland-s-defence, claim TL:ISL:event:1941:united-states-assumes-iceland-s-defence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Republic at Þingvellir
claims.summary: After an overwhelming referendum, Icelanders proclaimed a republic at Þingvellir, ending the union with Denmark; Sveinn Björnsson became the first president and 17 June became the national day.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1944-founding-of-the-republic-at-ingvellir, claim TL:ISL:event:1944:founding-of-the-republic-at-ingvellir, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Iceland a founding member of NATO
claims.summary: Abandoning neutrality, Iceland joined NATO as a founding member in 1949, a state with no army, on the understanding it would not host foreign troops in peacetime; the decision provoked a riot at the Althing.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1949, Vol. IV (Iceland and the North Atlantic Treaty)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1949-iceland-a-founding-member-of-nato, claim TL:ISL:event:1949:iceland-a-founding-member-of-nato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Cod War (12 nautical miles)
claims.summary: Iceland extended its fishery limit from four to twelve nautical miles in 1958; after confrontations at sea Britain acknowledged the twelve-mile limit, the first of Iceland's victories over the Royal Navy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1958-first-cod-war-12-nautical-miles, claim TL:ISL:event:1958:first-cod-war-12-nautical-miles, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Cod War (50 nautical miles)
claims.summary: Iceland extended its limit to fifty miles from September 1972; its coast guard cut dozens of British trawl nets before a NATO-mediated interim agreement was reached in November 1973.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1972-second-cod-war-50-nautical-miles, claim TL:ISL:event:1972:second-cod-war-50-nautical-miles, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Third Cod War (200 nautical miles)
claims.summary: Iceland claimed a 200-mile zone in 1975; after clashes and a threat to close the Keflavík NATO base, Britain recognised the 200-mile limit in an agreement of 2 June 1976.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1949, Vol. IV (Iceland and the North Atlantic Treaty)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1975-third-cod-war-200-nautical-miles, claim TL:ISL:event:1975:third-cod-war-200-nautical-miles, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 200-mile limit and the EEZ
claims.summary: Iceland's successful assertion of a 200-mile fishing zone helped establish the Exclusive Economic Zone in international law, later codified in the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-1976-the-200-mile-limit-and-the-eez, claim TL:ISL:event:1976:the-200-mile-limit-and-the-eez, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Collapse of the banks
claims.summary: The three big Icelandic banks, whose assets dwarfed the economy, failed within days in October 2008 in the largest banking collapse relative to GDP in history; the state passed emergency laws and turned to the IMF before recovering.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Iceland: From the Landnám and the world's oldest parliament to a volcanic republic that won its seas.", terralore.co/country/ISL/chronicle#ev-2008-collapse-of-the-banks, claim TL:ISL:event:2008:collapse-of-the-banks, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
